title: A walk that changes a remembered setting puts it back
goal: Two of the scripted walks only pass the first time they are ever run on a machine. One of them changes the text size from 24 to 48 and the app remembers that, so the next run looks for a 24 that is no longer there and stops. Anyone who runs the walks twice sees a failure that is not a real one, which makes the whole set less trustworthy to read.
notes: Found while regression-testing the colour picker walk work on 2026-09-04. type-menu-labels-walk step 17 is panelMenu {menu: 24 pt, choose: 48 pt}; the text size is remembered in the probe defaults, so on a second run the button reads 48 pt and the step fails with "no menu called 24 pt". drop-lands-here-walk has the same shape of problem from the other side: it carries a seed note saying to copy Scripts/playtest/fixtures/Photonz drop probe.png into ~/Pictures/Screenshots first, which nothing enforces, so it fails with "no tile called Photonz drop probe" unless a person read the note. Options: a reset step at the top of a walk, a walk-level setup block the runner performs, or the probe starting from clean defaults each launch.
acceptance: Running type-menu-labels-walk twice in a row passes both times
Running the whole walk set twice in a row produces the same result both times
Any walk that needs something set up first says so in a way the runner can act on, rather than only in a note for a person
